name: Maia chess (Maia-2, Maia-3)
usage: Human-like chess engine: predicts the move a player of a given rating would play; sparring partner, training

sources.note: Third-party safetensors conversion, 93 MB; source checkpoint hash equals the official one in CSSLab/maia2 model.py; original/model.pt is a pickle file
Official code and model, MIT; .pt on Google Drive
Maia-3, AGPLv3 (card text), .pt only, 316 MB; also Maia3-23M (51a0145a8178, 92 MB) and Maia3-5M (b6559de2398d, 21 MB). Exception needed

provenance.value: strong (Maia-2 copies): provenance.json gives the Google Drive source URL and the sha256 of the official checkpoint; tensors and the three model outputs checked equal with torch.equal; only the DataParallel 'module.' prefix removed
provenance.note: uploader affiliated with the University of Waterloo on Hugging Face; 25–32 downloads; the repository also holds original/model.pt (pickle); runtime chessnets or the official maia2 package

web.verdict: Well-liked human-like reference engine; Maia-3 best but AGPL, tactical blindness and UCI bugs; Maia-2 weak openings
web.summary: Maia predicts human moves (Maia-3 57.1 % move match vs 52.0 % for Maia-2, vendor). Players enjoy it as a sparring partner. Maia-2 was not trained on the first 5 plies, so its openings are poor (the website uses an opening book). Recent Maia-3 issues: misses simple tactics, fixed seed, monotonous weak play at high Elo locally, AGPL friction.
web.scope: Last 6 months plus launch discussions. HN comments, GitHub issues of CSSLab repos, HF discussions, TalkChess. Reddit and Lichess forum blocked.

comments.text: Launch post by the developer: Maia predicts the exact human move over 50 % of the time; meant as a sparring partner and teaching aid.
A 1560-rated player found it a real pleasure to play against, with human-like habits such as dropping pieces in complex exchanges.
Use it to find the mistakes a player at a given level would make and turn them into exercises; the developer says this is one of the goals.
Maia-2 shuffles knights back and forth in the opening; CSSLab: the first 5 plies were excluded from training.
Maia-2 training could not run outside CUDA on a Mac; fixed in July 2026, the README now lists Apple MPS.
Maia-3 launch: an effective drop-in replacement for the Leela Chess Zero model that outperformed the best existing LC0 model.
Maia-3 fails to predict what most players would play once a simple tactic (mate in 2) is on the board.
Maia-3 79M locally in En Croissant at Elo 2600 gave monotonous, weak play, unlike maiachess.com at the same level.
Maia-3 seed always 42 (identical games after restart), play collapses above Elo 2800, 'cp' scores are not centipawns.
The AGPL licence makes Maia-3 harder for others to use; several open issues ask CSSLab to clarify the checkpoint licence, unanswered.
Human-oriented analysis is better served by Maia's approach (a net trained on human moves) than by tuning Stockfish.
